line: e4 c5 Bc4 Nc6 f4 e6 Nf3 d5
teaches: A bishop developed early to the square that eyes f7 is committed before it knows what the centre will look like — the answer is the central pawn break played with TEMPO: it hits the bishop and the centre pawn in one move, so the piece that came out first is the piece that has to move twice.
explains: The pawn to d5 attacks the bishop on c4 and the pawn on e4 together. The bishop's diagonal is now a wall of its own making, and it has to retreat before anything else happens.
